slides.title: Questions-only timed practice
body: Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 1
Public Unit 1 revision sample · first session
slides.notes: This is timed formative practice, not a school-issued assessment or a grade predictor. Record actual time and exposure. The public questions/answers can be accessed beforehand, so freshness is never assumed.

slides.title: Confirm the practice conditions
body: Record whether you have seen these questions or answers.
Use questions only during the independent window.
Label any helped work as supported.
slides.notes: Use unit1-practice-record.md. If students have seen a question/model, record repeat practice or use a teacher-supplied changed version. No question-specific content is modelled in this deck. Support stops the independent clock for that work; do not combine supported and independent evidence.

slides.title: Reading time: 5 minutes
body: Open unit1-practice-paper.md only.
Read the instructions and plan your time.
Keep answers, examples and code execution closed.
slides.notes: Suggested reading allowance 5 minutes. The sample has 12 questions and suggests 55 working minutes. This split plan uses 40 working minutes today and 15 at the start of Lesson 2. Teachers may select a smaller section and record its scope/timing instead; do not imply a full paper was completed.

slides.title: Independent working time: first 20 minutes
body: Attempt the selected questions without help.
Show your reasoning and retain incomplete steps.
Keep the answer key closed.
slides.notes: Start the independent working clock. Hold this neutral slide; do not discuss paper Q3, show a trace or reveal question-specific hints. Teacher clarifications must not solve questions; record support and interruptions.

slides.title: Independent working time: next 20 minutes
body: Continue the same questions-only attempt.
Check your own working if time remains.
Keep corrections made now visible.
slides.notes: Continue to 40 working minutes in this session. This slide is a time cue, not a discussion break. No worked solution or compound-question model is shown before the attempt is preserved.

slides.title: Pause and preserve the original
body: Save or hand in your attempted version.
Record actual working time and unfinished questions.
Keep the key closed until Lesson 2’s attempt ends.
slides.notes: Pause the clock. Preserve the unedited response and note the stopping point. Follow the teacher’s storage/collection arrangement; do not complete questions at home before the continuation. A split session is not a continuous examination.

slides.title: Record exposure and support
body: Record help, interruptions or prior question exposure.
Separate supported work from independent work.
slides.notes: The record is a learning aid, not a score or authentication certificate. Prior-seen answers remain repeat practice even when the current window had no help. If a learner opens the key between sessions, record that exposure before continuing.

slides.title: Next lesson: continue before feedback
body: The next session starts with 15 working minutes.
No question-specific feedback is released yet.
slides.notes: Do not run an answer discussion as an exit activity. Keep uncertain steps for the continuation and later feedback. School conditions supersede this suggested practice arrangement.

lessons.title: Finish and preserve the attempt, then review
lessons.prepare: Continue the preserved attempt for 15 working minutes before any question-specific model or key. Stop and preserve the original responses before revealing feedback. Record actual combined time and prior exposure. Later corrections are supported; a changed retry is separate evidence. This split classroom activity is not a continuous formal examination. For practice use unit1-practice-paper.md, unit1-practice-answers.md only after closure, and unit1-practice-record.md. For a school task use only the school-issued materials.

slides.title: Finish the attempt before feedback
body: Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 2
Continue the preserved response with the key closed.
slides.notes: Check any exposure or help since Lesson 1. If the key has been viewed, label affected work repeat/supported; do not present it as a fresh continuation. This is public formative practice.

slides.title: Independent continuation: 15 minutes
body: Resume the chosen questions only.
Do not open answers or worked examples.
Stop when the teacher ends the window.
slides.notes: Suggested remaining working allowance 15 minutes, giving 55 working minutes across the two sessions after 5 reading minutes. Record actual duration; if a smaller section was selected, record that scope. No answer demonstration precedes this window.

slides.title: Stop and preserve all original responses
body: Stop the clock and preserve the attempted version.
Record unanswered parts and actual combined time.
The independent attempt is now closed.
slides.notes: This is the reveal boundary. Before advancing, every learner must preserve the original; if some are still attempting, hold here and keep examples/keys closed. A teacher who extends time must record it before feedback. Work completed after seeing feedback is supported correction, not independent completion.

slides.title: Feedback phase: compare, do not overwrite
body: Now open unit1-practice-answers.md.
Keep originals alongside explained corrections.
Identify the first mismatch and its cause.
slides.notes: Feedback starts only after closure. The reference key is public and allows equivalent valid reasoning; diagrams require teacher judgement. Record any self-check as practice evidence, not an official mark or grade prediction.

slides.title: Post-attempt Q3 trace
body: For [6, -2, 6], the first maximum stays at index 0.
The maximum is 6 and the total is 10.
Check for empty input before reading element zero.
slides.notes: This same-paper worked example is intentionally after the closed attempt. At i=1 the best remains 0; at i=2 equality does not replace the first maximum. Any new original-paper response written now is supported. Do not reuse it as fresh diagnostic evidence.

slides.title: Post-attempt Q9 explanation
body: Compare each layer name with its role or example.
A name-only response may miss part of the request.
slides.notes: After closure, pair Application with HTTPS/web service, Transport with TCP, Internet with IP and Network with Ethernet/Wi-Fi. Accept coherent alternatives. Keep the explanation separate from the original response and identify whether the issue was knowledge or interpreting the prompt.

slides.title: Changed retry: close the key
body: Trace the first maximum and total for [4, 9, 9, -1].
State the empty-input precaution in your own words.
Record this retry separately from the paper.
slides.notes: Key closed: first-maximum index 1, maximum 9, total 21. Changed values provide a new attempt but immediate transfer after teaching is not proof of durable mastery. If support is needed, label it and schedule another later changed retry.

slides.title: Keep the evidence phases separate
body: Original attempt: actual time, exposure and support.
Correction: explain the error and repaired rule.
Retry: show changed reasoning and a next step.
slides.notes: Use unit1-practice-record.md. Do not finish original questions after explanations and call that independent. Schedule a delayed changed retry in the existing revision/support time; no new graded task or homework requirement is added.
slides.strategy: Evidence review and next teaching step

lessons.title: Targeted practice with fresh examples
lessons.prepare: Open the exam-preparation chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

slides.title: Targeted practice with fresh examples
body: Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 3
Test a repaired idea beyond the original question.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Test a repaired idea beyond the original question. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Which correction needs a fresh test?
What feature should change while the rule stays the same?
slides.notes: Keep the underlying concept and change data or context. Examples include different negative values, a changed threshold or a new destination subnet. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Changed-data choices
slides.notes: Expected first maximum index 1/value -2; boundary checks -1,0,10,11; previous file records remain; remote subnet needs routing. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A first-maximum transfer
body: Trace [-9, -2, -2] using a strict > update.
Keep the index separate from the stored value.
slides.notes: Best index changes from 0 to 1 and stays 1 at equality. Starting maximum value at zero would fail for this all-negative list. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: The new boundary
body: The allowed whole-number range is 0 to 10.
Choose tests just outside and at both ends.
slides.notes: Useful tests are -1,0,1,9,10,11 and invalid text. Distinguish conversion failure from range rejection. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Choose two earlier weak ideas.
Create fresh tests and predict answers.
Complete them independently, then check explanations.
slides.notes: A partner can change values after the learner’s first prediction. Keep a concrete error/correction record for any remaining gap. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: Only positive lists were used to test a maximum search.
A: That proves an initial-zero algorithm is correct.
B: An all-negative case can reveal another fault.
slides.notes: B. Test families should challenge different assumptions, not repeat the same ordinary case. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Give one changed case and its result.
Explain why it checks your earlier misconception.
slides.notes: The explanation should connect the new data to the original faulty assumption or boundary. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Unit 1 review and future practice
body: Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 4
Explain key ideas and choose a realistic next step.
slides.notes: Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Explain key ideas and choose a realistic next step. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Retrieval and explanation
body: Explain one function result and one network path.
Name a reliable method for checking your reasoning.
slides.notes: Use short independent explanations. Accept traces, tests and requirement-based comparisons with clear assumptions. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Evidence across the unit
table: Trace and test a changed case
slides.notes: These examples support learning review. They do not certify complete syllabus coverage or predict a result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A realistic next action
body: Priority: distinguish local and remote traffic.
Action: trace two changed /24 destinations.
Later check: explain the gateway decision unaided.
slides.notes: A small specific action is easier to follow than revising everything. Use evidence from the earlier practice to choose it. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Peer explanation
body: Explain one corrected misconception without notes.
Invite a partner to change an assumption.
Revise the explanation if the change matters.
slides.notes: Example: change a mask, a tie rule or a file mode. Check the learner notices which conclusion depends on that assumption. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Independent practice
body: Complete a short mixed retrieval activity.
Write one independent programming explanation.
Write one network explanation and a later practice plan.
slides.notes: Use the textbook’s current practice questions. Any official examination instructions or school scheduling must come from the current authorised source, not this slide deck. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: A choice to explain
body: One successful sample means every skill is mastered.
A: Further changed examples can reveal gaps.
B: No further checking is useful.
slides.notes: A. Sampling gives limited evidence. Practical implementation, diagrams and later retrieval check different aspects. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

slides.title: Exit explanation
body: Name one idea you can explain clearly.
Choose one next practice action and when to retry it.
slides.notes: End with concrete progress and a realistic plan. Weeks 17–18 remain the planner’s examination block, with no new textbook lessons added here. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
